messages.content: What is the current Gini Coefficient of USA?

message.content:
The most recent widely‑cited estimate of the U.S. Gini coefficient comes from the World Bank’s World Development Indicators. According to that source, the Gini coefficient for the United States was **0.421 in 2019** (the latest year for which the World Bank publishes the figure).

> **World Bank (World Development Indicators)**  
> *Gini coefficient (World Bank estimate)* – 0.421 (2019)

> **Note:**  
> - The U.S. Census Bureau reports a higher Gini coefficient (≈ 0.485) for 2021, but it uses a different methodology (based on household income rather than consumption).  
> - OECD estimates for the U.S. are around 0.41–0.42 for the same period.  

So, depending on the source, the U.S. Gini coefficient is roughly between **0.41 and 0.48**, with the World Bank’s most recent figure being **0.421 (2019)**.
